summary.text: Ken Block is an independent candidate for governor. A software engineer and businessman, he founded the Moderate Party of Rhode Island, ran as its 2010 gubernatorial nominee (6.5%), sought the Republican nomination in 2014, and has been an independent since 2020. He campaigns on government accountability and cutting state fees.

paragraphs.text: Block was born in Milford, Connecticut, in 1965 and earned a B.S. from Dartmouth College.
A software engineer from Barrington, he founded Simpatico Software Systems in 2001, a data-mining company whose services government agencies and private businesses use to track waste and fraud.

Block founded the Moderate Party of Rhode Island, and a 2009 court battle he waged to gain it official state recognition made it easier for third parties to gather signatures and reach the ballot, according to Wikipedia.
He was the party's nominee for governor in 2010 and received 6.5 percent of the vote, finishing fourth in a four-way race.
He also served as president of RI Taxpayers, a taxpayer advocacy group, until May 2013.
His campaign website says he was a leading voice in the effort that led state lawmakers in 2013 to eliminate the "master lever" for straight-party voting.
In October 2013 Block announced he was joining the Republican Party to run for governor in 2014; he lost that primary to Cranston Mayor Allan Fung.
He has been an independent since 2020, and on April 2, 2026, he announced his third campaign for governor, this time as an independent.

His campaign website says he is running because of what he calls dysfunction and waste in state government and calls for making it more accountable, citing the state's $15 billion budget and the Washington Bridge.
